decisions.reason: Restricting filler-image placement to pages with huge empty spaces does not change the approved article typeface, weight, or readability constraints.
The filler-image placement rule does not change article category requirements, sources, allowed categories, or label presentation.
The general obligation to compile supplied materials according to the latest Flat Plan remains valid; the specific filler-image restriction is already owned by the source Requirement.
The source decision concerns filler images used for empty space and does not alter author names, photographs, sizing, sourcing, or placement.
The filler-image placement restriction does not affect the rule reserving red for the cover.
The polished, modern, brand-aligned style requirement remains unchanged by the page-specific filler-image placement instruction.
The source determines where supplied filler images may be inserted, not their quality or the existing remediation rule for low-quality article images.
The supplied tribute page remains required near the end of the magazine and is not identified as one of the filler images governed by the source decision.
The source decision does not change the inclusion or designer placement of articles listed on the cover but absent from the Flat Plan.
Restricting filler-image placement does not change the specified website as the source for magazine articles.
The current-issue filler-image placement rule does not alter the separate guidance requirement for avoiding white space in future issues.
The source refers to supplied filler images for huge empty spaces and does not modify the sharpness requirement for advertisements.
